inputs.title: docs(scope): fail closed when the visibility check's input is cut short
inputs.pr_body_part1:
`publish-scoping-pr.sh`'s public-content visibility check could let
private content through, in two places in the same guard. Under `set -uo
pipefail`, each unpushed scratch/ path was matched against the path list
with `printf "$WIP_PATHS" | grep -qxF`, and each blob was scanned with
`git cat-file -p | grep -Eq` inside an `if`. When the match came early
in input larger than a pipe buffer, grep exited while the writer was
still going, the writer died of SIGPIPE, and the pipeline's 141 read as
"no match". For the listing check that skipped the path unscanned. For
the blob scan it passed a blob that had a hit. Either way the push to
the public repository went ahead.

The path list and each blob now go to files in the script's scratch
directory, and grep's own status on the file decides. 0 is a match, 1 is
none, and anything else refuses, as does a failed `git cat-file`. The
guard fails closed. A scratch/ path that git prints quoted (unusual
characters) can't be read back by that name, so it now refuses instead
of passing unscanned. The failure message says so.

Two new cases in `publish-scoping-pr_test.sh` fail on the old code,
where the branch was pushed and a PR opened, and pass with the fix. One
commits a blob of about 760 KiB with a private reference on its first
line. The other commits 2,000 filler scratch/ files so the path list
outgrows a pipe buffer, with the offending path sorted first.
